newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices rise with colder weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices rise with colder weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices regained some strength Tuesday as forecasters called for colder temperatures by week's end in the central and northeast U.S., industry sources said.
Gulf Coast gas prices rose by a couple of cents into the $2.25-2.30 per million British thermal units range, with Transco (Station 65) deals done early in the mid-to-high-$2.30s.
A storm brewing in the western Caribbean may have also made buyers more wary of future gas supplies, sources said.
At 1100 EDT, the tropical depression was strengthening as it moved toward Cuba at a rate of 10 miles per hour.
In the Midcontinent, prices were up more than five cents to the $2.11-2.16 area as a cold front was expected to reach the region by Friday, tightening supplies.
In west Texas, Permian prices strengthened more than five cents to about the $2.12 area as demand escalated in south Texas. Similarly at Waha prices gained about four cents to the $2.13-2.18 range.

For Wednesday delivery, southern California border prices eased into the $2.04-2.09 range as cooler temperatures replaced last week's record heat. However, Day 1 prices (Thursday) remained strong in the high-teens to about $2.20.
Cooler weather in the Northeast helped to support prices at the New York city-gate where traders reported closing most deals in the mid-$2.60s.
